newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Olympic security expert gives C.Town thumbs up.
newsitem.headline: Olympic security expert gives C.Town thumbs up.

text.p: The head of security for last year's Atlanta Olympic Games, William Rathburn, said on Wednesday he was confident Cape Town could provide a safe environment for the Olympic Games.
"I probably have more confidence that Cape Town can provide a safe environment for the Olympics than the people who live here do," he told a news conference.
Rathburn, who has been in the country for two weeks, was invited by the Cape Town 2004 Bid Company to assess the security needs and planning.
"Providing security for Olympics is difficult. You have to put a lot of effort, time and resources into it -- but it is doable," he said.
"It would be easier for Cape Town than Los Angeles and Atlanta because there is a national police force. We had in excess of 50 law enforcement agencies with no one person in charge to deal with."
Rathburn admitted he had noticed a high level of crime reported in Cape Town, but added: "I would guess that most of the crime is neighbourhood orientated, as it is in any major city of the world.
"I don't doubt that crime is a major problem in Cape Town...I am also certain it is a problem in Rome, Athens, Buenos Aires and even Stockholm. It is not a problem that is limited to South Africa."
Rathburn, who has met Police Minister Sydney Mufamadi, national police commissioner George Fivaz and Bid Company officials, said he was impressed by the "receptive attitude" experienced in Cape Town.

"Some cities have the attitude that they know it all and don't need assistance. There is a long tradition of previous host cities helping the next but it is only successful if there is a receptive attitude."
He said he had not been invited to the four other cities -- Athens, Buenos Aires, Rome, Stockholm -- bidding for the 2004 Olympic Games. The host city will be announced on September 5.
